1About this guide

This guide is for the M&E officers of the Africa CDC Results-Based Management (RBM) platform. M&E keeps the indicators and their links to the workplan, follows the flow of every Business Unit (BU), and signs off the quarterly results:

You…WhereChapter
Keep the T1 to T4 indicators and their targetsPIRS › Indicators3
Link T3/T4 indicators to broad and specific activitiesPIRS › Activity Mapping4
Follow the specific activities of every BU and their approvalM&E › Review Submissions, the activity page5
Sign off the quarterly reportsM&E › Review Submissions › Quarterly Reports6
Follow the activity reports of every BUM&E › Review Submissions › Activity Reports7
Find the records that hold up a workflowM&E › Data Health9

Specific activities and activity reports are approved by the Responsible Person of the Business Unit (usually the head of division or director), called the Responsible Person in this guide: the person named for each Business Unit in the org structure. Focal persons and Responsible Persons have their own guides.

The guide follows the platform as it works on 7 November 2026. The screen captures come from the platform itself, filled with sample data: names, activities and figures are examples.

Where to find this guide

Click User guides, the last entry of the main menu: Open reads the guide of a role in the browser, Download saves the PDF. Help, at the right end of the menu, opens this guide on the chapter about the page you are on (on a phone: Help on this page, at the top of the menu).

The tour

At your first sign-in, a short tour of the screen opens on your home page; each step points at a part of the screen. Next and Back move from step to step; Skip the tour or the Escape key closes it. To take it again: your initials › Take the tour.

2Your menu and the selectors

Click Sign in with Microsoft and use your Africa CDC account, the same one as Outlook and Teams. There is no separate password for the platform.

If your session ends, sign in again: you come back to the page you were on. No RBM account matches this Microsoft account means you chose another account, or you need access: Request access writes to the RBM team (pra@africacdc.org).

Your menu is organised by area. An area with several pages is a dropdown, for example PIRS.

Top menuItemsWhat it opens
DashboardThe overview of every Business Unit.
Country WorkplanThe activities planned in a country that has a country office (chapter 8).
Project ▾Project Proposal, Impacts (T1), Outcomes (T2), Broad Activities, Workplan, Short Term Outcome / Output, Specific ActivitiesThe results framework and the workplan of every Business Unit.
LogframeThe logical framework.
PIRS ▾IndicatorsThe Performance Indicator Reference Sheets (chapter 3).
Activity MappingLink T3/T4 indicators to activities (chapter 4).
Contributions ReportEach indicator with the activities that contribute to it (chapter 4).
M&E ▾Review SubmissionsSubmissions of every Business Unit, and your sign-off queue (chapters 5 to 7).

Reporting ▾Big Tickets, Quarterly Dashboard, Donors & Reports, Monthly DigestReporting views (chapter 10).
Strategic PlanThe reference strategic plan.
User guidesThe guide of each role, to read in the browser or download as PDF (chapter 1).

Two roles? If you are also the focal person or the Responsible Person of a Business Unit, the pages of that role are gathered in one dropdown called BU, right after Dashboard.

You see every Business Unit

Your role reads the plan and the reports of every BU. The BU selector on the right of the top bar only lists the Business Units you belong to yourself (it is hidden if you belong to one or none): you do not need it to see the other Business Units. If you pick one of your BUs in it, the PIRS page shows that BU only; on All my divisions it shows every BU.

The year selector

The year selector chooses the fiscal year. Planning pages (PIRS, Activity Mapping, the workplan, the Country Workplan) follow it. A year not started yet carries the label PLANNING; reporting pages such as Review Submissions then show “FY2027 has not started” with a Switch to FY2026 button.

3PIRS indicators

Open PIRS › Indicators. The page Performance Indicator Reference Sheets lists the indicators of the selected year as they are in the PIRS, for every Business Unit, with the number of indicators, how many have a baseline and how many have a target.

  • Click a tier card (T1 Impact, T2 Outcome, T3 Short-term Outcome, T4 Output) to show that tier only, or search by name, code or definition.
  • To see the activities that contribute to an indicator, open the Contributions Report (chapter 4).
  • The menu at the end of a row offers View details, Edit and Delete. The detail page shows the definition, the methodology, the data collection, the targets and the linked activities.
  • Export downloads the PIRS of the year; New Indicator opens a blank indicator form.

The indicator form

New Indicator and Edit open the same page, in sections:

SectionMain fields
Indicator IdentityIndicator Code *, Tier *, Category, AHSS Pillar, Indicator Name *, Definition
ClassificationLinked Outcome Area, Unit of Measure
MeasurementNumerator, Denominator, Baseline Value, Baseline Source
TargetsThe annual targets of each year (the current one is marked), the Q1 to Q4 targets of the year, the overall target
Reporting PeriodsThe quarters in which a report is expected, year by year, with quick choices (all quarters, annual, semi-annual…)
Data Collection & ReportingData source and method, reporting frequency and level, disaggregation, Accountable Division (the main Business Unit) and Contributing Divisions

Click Create Indicator or Save Changes. If the four quarterly targets do not add up to the annual target, the form warns you; you can still save.

The 2027 indicators come from the PIRS version 7.0: each T3/T4 indicator belongs to the BU named as primary responsible. The annual targets of every T3/T4 indicator are set in the PIRS. The focal person of the BU reviews them with the other staff of the division and gets the approval of the head of division; if something is inconsistent, the focal person contacts M&E to discuss it and make the corrections. The quarterly targets entered for the BU decide in which quarters a report is expected: a quarter with a target above 0 expects one.

4Activity Mapping

Activity Mapping links the T3/T4 indicators to the activities that contribute to them. Open PIRS › Activity Mapping. The page follows the year selector.

Step 1: Choose what to map

  • Broad Activities or Specific Activities: a broad activity can contribute to several Tier 3 / Tier 4 indicators; a specific activity contributes to one.
  • Search by code, title or Business Unit, and filter All, Linked or Unlinked to find the activities still without an indicator.

Step 2: Add or remove a link

  • Click Add a T3/T4 indicator… in the row, type to filter, and pick the indicator. For a specific activity that already has one, the box reads Change indicator… and replaces it.
  • Click the × on a chip to remove a link.
  • There is no Save button: each change is saved at once, and the message Indicator links saved confirms it.

Where the links are used

  • The Contributions Report (PIRS › Contributions Report) reads these links. It lists each indicator with the activities linked to it, their Business Unit and their budget. Switch between broad and specific activities, and between T3 and T4.
  • The specific activity form does not use them. When a focal person picks a broad activity, the Linked Indicator (T3/T4) list offers the T3/T4 indicators of the broad activity's Business Unit, or those of the focal person's own Business Units when it has none.

Only M&E and administrators change the links. Other users see the page read-only.

5Following the specific activities of every BU

Activities waiting for a decision

Open M&E › Review Submissions (on the current year), tab Specific Activities. You see every activity In Review of every Business Unit and of every fiscal year; the FY column tells the year. Use the search and the directorate and division filters to follow one Business Unit.

The decision on a specific activity belongs to the Responsible Person of its Business Unit. Your role is to see where each one stands: click the eye button to open the activity.

The Approval trail

The activity page ends with the Approval trail: the date, the person and the event (Created as draft, Edited, Submitted for approval, Approved, Rejected with the reason in quotes, Edited, sent back for approval, Cancelled). While the activity is in review, the first line names whom it waits for.

If the line reads Waiting for: nobody: ask your administrator to name one in Org Structure, neither the Business Unit nor the ones above it have a Responsible Person named, and nobody can decide. Ask the administrator to name one in Org Structure.

The whole plan of a Business Unit

Project › Specific Activities and Project › Workplan show the activities of every Business Unit for the selected year.

Planning an activity yourself

On Project › Specific Activities, New activity opens the same form as the focal persons, with one Save button. An activity you create is approved at once, without review; its trail reads Created and approved (administrator).

StatusWhat it means
DraftSaved but not submitted. Drafts stay private until you submit. Everything can still change.
In ReviewSubmitted. The Responsible Person of the Business Unit decides. It cannot be edited from the list while it waits.
ApprovedPart of the workplan of the Business Unit. It shows in the Workplan and, if its place is a country with a country office, in the Country Workplan.
RejectedSent back with a reason. Edit it and submit it again.
CancelledWithdrawn from the workplan. It stays in the list for the record.

6Signing off the quarterly reports

Where your sign-off comes in

Every quarterly (indicator) report ends with the step M&E / Admin Sign-off:

Report written bySteps
The main Business Unit of the indicator (role OWNER)M&E / Admin Sign-off.
A contributing Business Unit (role CONTRIBUTOR)The Responsible Person of the contributing Business Unit, then the Responsible Person of the main Business Unit, then M&E / Admin Sign-off.

The sign-off goes to the M&E officer of the Business Unit (the nearest one up the org structure). When the Business Unit has none, it goes to every M&E officer: the queue then reads Any M&E officer, and any of them can sign it off.

Step 1: Your queue

Open M&E › Review Submissions, tab Quarterly Reports, and pick the quarter.

  • Awaiting Your Approval: the reports at your step, marked Assigned to you or Any M&E officer.
  • All Reports: every indicator report of every division for the quarter, with its role, status and current step. Use the status chips (All, Draft, In review, Approved, Rejected) and Report expected to see who has not reported yet.

Step 2: Open the report and decide

Click Review →. Read the result, the narrative, the challenges, the recommendations and the files, then:

  • Approve: the report becomes Approved and counts in the dashboards and exports.
  • Reject: write a reason (required). The report goes back to its Business Unit to be fixed and submitted again.

Admin override forces a status (for example reopens an approved report). Use it only to correct a mistake: it is recorded in the Workflow Timeline.

Several reports at once, exports and reminders

  • Tick reports in Awaiting Your Approval, then Approve selected › Approve <n>.
  • Quarterly report Qx and Activity reports Qx download the reports of the quarter (Excel or CSV).
  • Remind draft reporters sends a reminder to the authors of reports still in draft.

7Activity reports and ownership disputes

The tab Activity Reports of Review Submissions shows the activity reports of every Business Unit: Submitted (waiting for a decision) or Drafts. Each row has an Actions menu with View Details.

  • A report written by the Business Unit of the activity is approved by its Responsible Person.
  • A report written by a Business Unit contributing to the activity goes through the Responsible Person of that Business Unit, then the Responsible Person of the activity's Business Unit, then M&E / Admin Sign-off.

The tab Ownership Disputes lists the items a Business Unit flagged as not its own (for example with Flag ownership dispute on a specific activity), so they can be given to the right Business Unit.

8Country Workplan

Country Workplan lists every specific activity located in one country, whatever the Business Unit that plans it, for the selected year. Only countries that have an Africa CDC country office have a Country Workplan.

  • Pick the country at the top right. The list offers the countries that have a country office and activities that year; with one country, there is no picker.
  • It shows the activities Approved, In Execution, Closed or In Review whose location is exactly the country. Drafts never appear.
  • The members of a country office see the activities to be conducted in their country.
  • A country office also plans its own activities: they are carried by the office, set in its country, approved by the Responsible Person of the office, and they appear here once submitted.

A new country office is created by an administrator in Org Structure: a new Business Unit with Country office ticked and the African Union Member State chosen. Its director and members are added as usual; they then see the Country Workplan of their country.

9Data Health

Some records hold up a workflow until someone completes them: a Business Unit without its Responsible Person sends its approvals elsewhere, and a broad activity without an indicator link counts toward no indicator. Open M&E › Data Health. The page Data Health <year> runs ten checks on the year of the year selector and lists the records to complete.

Each check gives its count, or Complete when nothing is left, and says why it matters. Click a row to open the page where the record is fixed; a long list shows 15 rows at a time (Show … more). Org Structure and Users & Roles are administrator pages: if you cannot open them, send the rows to an administrator.

CheckWhere it is fixed
Business units without their peopleThe Business Unit in Org Structure: the row says who is missing (Responsible Person, M&E officer or focal person).
Country offices without a focal personThe country office in Org Structure.
Broad activities without a budget codeThe page of the broad activity.
Broad activities not linked to an indicatorPIRS › Activity Mapping, Broad Activities (chapter 4).
Approved specific activities without an indicatorThe page of the specific activity; or link it in PIRS › Activity Mapping, Specific Activities.
T3/T4 indicators without a Business UnitThe indicator form: Accountable Division (chapter 3).
T3/T4 indicator codes with a space or a double dot, or used twice in the yearThe indicator form: Code (chapter 3).
Active users without a unitUsers & Roles.
Fund centres of the budget execution not linked to an activityThe page Budget codes not linked to an activity.

The weekly email

Every Monday, when a check is not complete, the M&E officers and the RBM administrators receive Data to complete this week: the current year, and the next one once its plan is in the platform, at most 10 rows per check, with an Open Data health button.

10Reporting views

PageWhat it shows
Reporting › Quarterly DashboardReporting completeness per division for a quarter: Total Divisions, Fully Reported, On Track, Missing Baselines, Missing Targets, Needs Attention, and a table of the divisions, with Division summary and Export quarterly.
Reporting › Big TicketsThe leadership priorities of the year, grouped by AHSS pillar, with the status and performance of the chosen quarter. M&E can create a Big Ticket, report on behalf of a Business Unit, and approves Big Ticket reports.
Reporting › Donors & ReportsThe funding sources of the plan year, from the budget codes. Open one to see what it funds, by Business Unit and by budget code.
Reporting › Monthly DigestThe situation of a directorate and of its Business Units (below).

Monthly Digest

Reporting › Monthly Digest shows the situation of a directorate and of every Business Unit under it: the specific activities of the year by status, the items waiting more than 7 days for a decision, the high-risk activities, the activity reports and quarterly indicator reports of the reporting quarter by status, and the budget execution of each Business Unit. If your role reads every dashboard, pick the directorate in the list at the top right.

The page shows the situation on the day you open it. Print or save as PDF prints it on A4; in the print window, choose to save as PDF to keep a copy. On the first day of each month, the Responsible Person of each directorate receives it by email.

Report statuses

StatusWhat it means
Not startedNo report has been opened for this activity or indicator yet.
DraftStarted and saved, not yet submitted.
SubmittedSubmitted. It waits for the decision of the reviewer.
In reviewAn indicator or activity report on its way through its approval steps.
ApprovedAccepted. It now counts in the dashboards and exports.
RejectedSent back with a reason. Fix it and submit it again.
N/AMarked “not applicable”: no report is expected for this item this quarter.

Need help? Contact the PR&A team for the plan and the org structure, and the Software Developer Unit for the platform. This guide reflects the platform as configured on 7 November 2026; screens evolve as it is improved.
